Class PwmServoShield

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.device.servo.PwmServoShield
public final class PwmServoShield extends Object
The "16 x 12-bit PWM & Servo Shield": an NXP PCA9685 that generates sixteen servo signals on its own, driven over I2C as plain Java on top of I2c (so it needs no Arduino library). A servo is just a channel number, 0..15, so nothing is allocated after the shield itself: 
PwmServoShield shield = new PwmServoShield(ArduinoUno.getI2c(), PwmServoShield.ADDRESS_DEFAULT); // once, at startup
shield.write(0, 90);          // servo on channel 0 to its centre
shield.writeMicros(1, 1500);  // or a raw pulse width
shield.release(0);            // stop driving it; the servo no longer holds its position

write(int, int) takes the same 0..180 degrees as Servo.write(int) and maps them onto the same pulse widths the Arduino Servo library uses, 544 to 2400 microseconds, so a program moves from an onboard pin to the shield without changing its angles.

The servos are powered from the shield's green terminal block (5-6V), never from the board: its V+ pins are fed only from there. Each channel is a column of three pins, GND nearest the board edge, V+ in the middle and PWM nearest the chip, matching a servo's brown, red and yellow wires. The shield answers at address 0x40; bridging its address pads selects another, passed to the constructor. Works on every board, wherever Wire reaches the shield's SDA/SCL. The constructor accepts a given I2c so a unit test can mock the bus.
